message.content: The contract requires exact once-rounded FP16 bit patterns over the entire finite FP16 domain. I'll record the highest-risk, directly testable claims for the probe phase.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "libdevice.exp and div_rn introduce up to ~1 ulp FP64 error before the single cvt.rn.f16.f64 rounding; if a computed FP64 value lands on the wrong side of an FP16 halfway boundary relative to the exact real sigmoid, the output bit pattern will differ from the contract's once-rounded requirement. The full finite FP16 input domain is only 65536 values, so an exhaustive bit-pattern comparison against a high-precision (e.g. mpmath) correctly rounded reference is feasible and decisive.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Each output must be the exact real sigmoid value rounded ONCE to IEEE binary16 with round-to-nearest, ties-to-even; 'Exact FP16 bit patterns ... must hold for the whole public domain' and 'Every finite FP16 encoding is legal'."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract demands exact RNE-once bit patterns for every finite FP16 input (\"Every finite FP16 encoding is legal... One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation\"), so a full sweep over all 65536 finite FP16 encodings is the decisive in-scope test.", "statement": "For at least one finite FP16 input, the kernel's FP64 intermediate rounding (libdevice.exp ~1 ulp + div_rn + cvt.rn.f16.f64 double rounding) produces an FP16 output bit pattern different from the exact real sigmoid(x) rounded once to binary16 RNE."}

function.arguments: {"rationale": "Sigmoid underflows binary16 below ~2^-25, i.e. x > ~17.5; several FP16 inputs exceed this, and the strict subnormal RNE behavior near 2^-24/2^-25 is where simple formula evaluations most often snap incorrectly. Similarly x < -11.1 must give 0.9995 (1-2^-11). A domain sweep should explicitly verify these tail encodings and subnormal FP16 inputs.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "The contract explicitly requires: both input zeros give 0.5; positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero; subnormals and the largest finite values are legal inputs with exact bit-pattern outputs."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract explicitly pins these extremes: \"positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero\", and \"Every finite FP16 encoding is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and the largest positive and negative finite values.\"", "statement": "The kernel mishandles the extreme tails of the legal FP16 domain: for large positive x (e.g. x=+65504 or any x above ~17.5) it may emit a nonzero subnormal or wrong bit pattern instead of exact +0.0 (0x0000), and for large negative x it may fail to produce exactly 1-2^-11 (0x3B80) or the correct rounding for subnormal inputs near the FP16-tie region."}
